packs.title: Across the City
packs.promise: Explore ranch materials, wetland clues, art and coastal shapes.

q.s: Collect textures from a historic house and its garden.
st: From an open visitor area, find one house surface, one garden texture and one feature that connects indoor and outdoor space. Collect observations only.
Describe how the three differ: rough or smooth, repeated or irregular, sheltered or exposed. Keep your descriptions tied to visible details.
Arrange your three descriptions as a small material palette. Choose one pairing and explain what you would notice first if you returned.

q.s: Follow an open nature path and track three transitions.
st: At the trail entrance, choose a permitted out-and-back or open signed loop that you can comfortably finish before closing. Notice the first view before moving.
Walk at an easy pace. Stop out of the walking line at three changes in light, vegetation or water visibility; do not leave the trail to find a better view.
After your walk, draw a three-stop sequence or write three short descriptions in walking order. Describe one change that movement revealed.

q.s: Create a small composition from beach, water and sky.
st: Choose a safe stationary view where beach, water and sky form separate bands. Keep circulation clear and use an allowed public path if sand is unsuitable.
Make an original three-band drawing or three short lines of text. Let one band dominate and add a detail you actually saw to each.
Give your composition a title and explain why you chose that balance. It can be entirely written; do not photograph dogs or owners as your proof.

packs.title: Civic Center to the Harbor
packs.promise: Explore civic details, downtown architecture and the harbor’s open edges.

q.s: Create a façade study from the sidewalk.
st: Choose a public sidewalk view of the library façade. Find a glass section, a wood element and a gap or opening in the composition.
Draw the relationship of those three, or write three lines that vary in length to match what you see. Keep your work original rather than tracing a sign or logo.
Explain which material appears to hold the composition together. One clear relationship is enough.

q.s: Pause beside a lagoon without crossing its bridges.
st: Choose a stable permitted stopping place where you can see water and a bridge or island edge.
Look for a reflection, ripple or light change for several quiet minutes. If the surface gives no clear reflection, keep a water-and-edge observation instead.
Write two short notes: what held still in your view and what changed. Add one visible shape that links the two.

q.s: Create an original pattern from a waterfront village.
st: Choose a permitted boardwalk viewpoint and find three colors or repeated shapes in the built scene. Avoid making signs, logos or strangers the subject.
Create an original rhythm with those details: a small pattern drawing, a repeating three-word line or a short color sequence with notes.
Break the rhythm once using a detail from the harbor view. Explain which part now feels most like this place.
